chosen_protocol_summary: BASIS COARSENING of x_proj with an LS refit, asymmetric per projection family. Three nested ops, all from the trained checkpoint, NO TRAINING: (1) blocksum-LS -- replace trained x_proj by its exact block-sum init B (sparse_modeling.py:883-886) and re-fit SLoRB_Weight by least squares in the new basis; x_proj becomes parameter-free. (2) coarsen -- additionally k -> k*c, exactly the branch that training with SLoRB_k = k*c would have used as a basis; LS-optimal coefficient for the coarser basis is the block MEAN of the c adjacent columns, NOT the sum (summing inflates scale by c). (3) asymmetric -- a different c per projection family, justified by measured per-family cost/damage: down_proj holds 22.28% of SLoRB_Weight yet has the LOWEST relE/W_eff (median 0.1546) and the lowest coarsening perturbation at every c, with o_proj next (0.1806).

must_not_claim: That a post-hoc truncation of a trained branch is a TRAINING-TIME rank ablation. Every rung is surgery on model_best_lm_eval.pt at iter_num 17900. A model trained from scratch with SLoRB_k=128 could reallocate capacity during training and land anywhere, plausibly BETTER than this ladder's rung at the same density. This experiment cannot bound that. The supportable claim is 'the trained branch contains this much extractable redundancy'; it may NEVER be phrased as 'SLoRB only needs rank r' or 'SparseForge should be trained with SLoRB_k = ...'.
That the 5.3657 pp window is 'the value of SLoRB'. It is folded-dense vs true-2:4. The honest variant-matched +/-SLoRB contrast is -2.4515 pp, i.e. +SLoRB is WORSE.

Any placement of any rung, or of R0, in a 2:4 column, table or sentence. All are folded and dense on disk (R0 linear_zero_ratio 1.08e-9). The existing bar at logs/sparseforge_tm_union9_slorb_progress.log:314 is ADVISORY ONLY with zero programmatic enforcement, so this is a human obligation.

load_bearing_question_answer.question: whether 'block-basis coarsening of a low-rank branch bolted onto 2:4-sparse weights' is distinct from generic post-hoc adapter-rank reduction
load_bearing_question_answer.answer: DISTINCT -- but on FOUR conjuncts, not the five claimed in RELATED_WORK.md sec 6, and the strongest reason is the AXIS rather than the operator.
load_bearing_question_answer.primary_reason_axis: Generic post-hoc rank reduction minimises adapter STORAGE at fixed quality. B12 titrates DEPLOYMENT DENSITY in the two-matmul form, against a hard floor of 50.0% (pure 2:4, zero branch) and a ceiling of 63.1011%. On a DENSE base that quantity does not exist -- shrinking an adapter moves storage but not the base's arithmetic density. The axis is a consequence of the base being N:M. Measured, not asserted: rung A gives back 6.85 density points (63.1011 -> 56.2500) at live_branch_params exactly 404,750,336.
load_bearing_question_answer.secondary_reason_operator: Every surface-(a) work found is SVD/spectral and stores BOTH factors. B12's coarse basis is a zero-parameter block indicator whose LS refit is closed-form (a block mean), exact because on-block entries are precisely 1.0 (sparse_modeling.py:886; re-measured min == max == 1.0).
load_bearing_question_answer.tertiary_reason_nobody_reduced_a_trained: SLoPe ADDS lazily; SLiM CONSTRUCTS one-shot; ARMOR CONSTRUCTS multiplicative wrappers; HASSLE-free DECOMPOSES a dense matrix; Shears and LoSA allocate rank DURING training. 37 independent queries aimed at the conjunction returned zero occupants.
load_bearing_question_answer.CONJUNCT_3_MUST_BE_NARROWED: RELATED_WORK.md sec 6 conjunct 3 says 'the literature's post-hoc adapter operator is uniformly SVD/spectral'. Against ARMOR (ICLR 2026) that is FALSE AS STATED -- ARMOR is post-training, block-structured, on a 2:4 core. It is true only under the restriction 'applied to a trained adapter'. Conjunct 3 is therefore narrowed to: block-basis coarsening OF A TRAINED ADAPTER is not in the literature. Stated generally it would overclaim against a published paper.
load_bearing_question_answer.two_further_honesty_items: (i) The ALGEBRAIC FORM 'exactly-2:4 base + additive low-rank term, deployed' is prior art via HASSLE-free -- B12 must not present that form as its own. (ii) BLOCK STRUCTURE PER SE is prior art via ARMOR and arXiv:2510.23346.
load_bearing_question_answer.asymmetry_claim_has_one_more_competitor: The file compares its pre-registered per-family map only to PARA (emergent from a global threshold) and OWL (sparsity axis). LoSA also does non-uniform per-layer adapter rank from measured reconstruction error, ON A SPARSE BASE. B12's asymmetry is still distinguishable (pre-registered from an exhaustive 5^7 frontier scan, on the basis-WIDTH axis, post hoc) but must now be stated against LoSA too.
load_bearing_question_answer.surviving_delta: Post-hoc reduction of an ALREADY-TRAINED low-rank branch on an EXACTLY-2:4 base, via a zero-parameter block-indicator basis with a closed-form LS refit, titrated against a deployment-density axis that only exists because the base is N:M. Four conjuncts: (1) exactly-2:4 base measured over all 224 tensors, 0 violations; (2) branch genuinely trained then reduced with no retraining; (3) zero-parameter coarse basis with closed-form LS refit -- NARROWED to 'applied to a trained adapter'; (4) deployment-density axis against a 50.0% hard floor.
